questions.q: Why does gypsum board contribute to fire resistance?
o: It contains structural steel mesh in all cases
It has no water in its chemistry
Its chemically combined water absorbs heat as it is driven off as steam
questions.ref: ASTM C1396/C1396M - Standard Specification for Gypsum Board
questions.n: Gypsum contains chemically combined water; calcination during heating consumes heat and delays temperature rise through the assembly.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sealant joint between dissimilar cladding materials?
o: To maintain weather tightness while accommodating differential movement
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated - exterior finishes, sealants, insulation and fire-protection assemblies
questions.n: Sealant joints are detailed to keep out water and air while allowing relative movement between adjoining materials.

questions.q: Why is EIFS often called synthetic stucco?
o: Because its exterior finish resembles stucco but is part of a layered insulation-and-finish system
Because it is made only of fired clay
questions.ref: EIFS Industry Members Association (EIMA), EIFS terminology and system guidance
questions.n: EIFS uses polymer-modified base and finish coats over insulation, producing a stucco-like appearance without being traditional portland-cement stucco.

questions.q: A steel column must retain load-carrying capacity longer during a fire without being boxed in with board protection. Which coating system is appropriate?
questions.ref: UL Solutions, Firestop and Perimeter Fire Containment Systems guidance
questions.n: Intumescent coatings provide a thin decorative-looking finish that expands into an insulating char under fire exposure.

questions.q: Which sealant family is widely used for durable exterior construction joints and has good adhesion to many building substrates?
questions.ref: ASTM C920 - Standard Specification for Elastomeric Joint Sealants
questions.n: Polyurethane is a common high-performance elastomeric sealant for exterior building joints.

questions.q: A curtain wall passes the edge of a fire-rated floor slab, leaving a continuous perimeter gap. What system is needed at that gap?
o: A tested perimeter fire-containment / safing system
questions.ref: ASTM E2307 - Standard Test Method for Determining Fire Resistance of Perimeter Fire Barriers
questions.n: The slab-edge gap must be protected by a tested perimeter fire-containment system to limit vertical fire and smoke spread.

questions.q: What is safing in a curtain-wall/fire-barrier context?
o: Fire-resistant material installed at the slab edge/perimeter joint to limit fire and smoke spread
questions.ref: ASTM E2307 - Standard Test Method for Determining Fire Resistance of Perimeter Fire Barriers
questions.n: Safing insulation and related perimeter fire-containment components protect the void between a floor slab edge and curtain wall.

questions.q: Which property most distinguishes an elastomeric sealant used in movement joints?
o: It can deform and recover as the joint opens and closes
It permanently locks both sides together
It carries all structural gravity loads
questions.ref: ASTM C920 - Standard Specification for Elastomeric Joint Sealants
questions.n: Elastomeric sealants are formulated to accommodate cyclic joint movement while maintaining adhesion and weather resistance.

questions.q: What is the principal function of an intumescent coating on structural steel?
o: To delay steel temperature rise during fire exposure
questions.ref: UL Solutions, Firestop and Perimeter Fire Containment Systems guidance
questions.n: The expanded char insulates steel and delays heating, helping the member retain strength for the required fire-resistance period.

questions.q: What is the chemical composition of gypsum?
questions.ref: ASTM C1396/C1396M - Standard Specification for Gypsum Board
questions.n: Natural gypsum is calcium sulfate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

questions.q: Which standard is used for fire-resistive joint systems in building assemblies?
questions.ref: ASTM E1966 - Standard Test Method for Fire-Resistive Joint Systems
questions.n: ASTM E1966 is a fire-test method for fire-resistive joint systems.

questions.q: Which layer in EIFS provides the primary continuous thermal insulation?
questions.ref: EIFS Industry Members Association (EIMA), EIFS terminology and system guidance
questions.n: EIFS incorporates continuous insulation board, typically foam plastic, between the substrate and reinforced base coat.

questions.q: Two exterior facade panels undergo thermal movement in opposite directions. What joint material should bridge the gap while maintaining weather resistance?
questions.ref: ASTM C920 - Standard Specification for Elastomeric Joint Sealants
questions.n: An elastomeric sealant can stretch and compress while maintaining adhesion and weather tightness.

questions.q: What does refractory mean in construction-material terminology?
o: Highly elastic at room temperature only
Capable of resisting high temperatures without unacceptable deterioration
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - paint, sealant, fireproofing and finish terminology
questions.n: A refractory material is designed to withstand high-temperature exposure while retaining useful properties.

questions.q: What happens to an intumescent coating when exposed to high heat?
o: It expands to form an insulating char
questions.ref: UL Solutions, Firestop and Perimeter Fire Containment Systems guidance
questions.n: Intumescent coatings swell dramatically when heated and form a low-density insulating char that protects the substrate.

questions.q: Which paint component is typically the volatile liquid carrier that evaporates during drying?
questions.ref: Paint and Coating Testing Manual / architectural coatings terminology; ASTM D16 - Standard Terminology for Paint, Related Coatings, Materials, and Applications
questions.n: In conventional solvent-borne paint, the solvent is the volatile component that reduces viscosity and evaporates as the film forms.

questions.q: What is firestopping?
o: A system used to restore the fire-resistance continuity of penetrations and joints in rated assemblies
questions.ref: NFPA fire-protection guidance and listed firestop/perimeter fire-containment systems
questions.n: Firestop systems seal penetrations and joints so the fire-resistance rating of floors and walls is maintained.

questions.q: Which general coating family is traditionally suitable for properly prepared galvanized-iron roofing when compatibility with the zinc surface is addressed?
o: Alkyd or specially formulated metal-roof coating
questions.ref: AMPP/SSPC protective-coatings guidance for metal substrates
questions.n: Galvanized steel requires a coating system compatible with zinc and properly prepared; alkyd or dedicated metal-roof coatings are common traditional choices.

questions.q: What does EIFS stand for?
questions.ref: EIFS Industry Members Association (EIMA), EIFS terminology and system guidance
questions.n: EIFS is the standard abbreviation for Exterior Insulation and Finish System.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes passive fire protection from active fire protection?
o: Passive systems are unrelated to rated walls
Passive systems are only portable extinguishers
Passive systems are built into assemblies to resist or limit fire spread without needing activation by occupants
questions.ref: NFPA fire-protection guidance and listed firestop/perimeter fire-containment systems
questions.n: Passive fire protection includes rated assemblies, firestopping, and protective coatings that perform as part of the construction.

questions.q: What is the primary role of the binder in paint?
o: To form the continuous film and bind pigment to the substrate
To act solely as a volatile carrier
questions.ref: Paint and Coating Testing Manual / architectural coatings terminology; ASTM D16 - Standard Terminology for Paint, Related Coatings, Materials, and Applications
questions.n: The binder or resin forms the paint film and holds pigment particles together and to the substrate.

questions.q: Which of these is commonly considered a high-performance elastomeric building sealant type?
questions.ref: ASTM C920 - Standard Specification for Elastomeric Joint Sealants
questions.n: Silicone sealants are widely used as high-movement, weather-resistant architectural joint sealants.

questions.q: What is the primary role of pigment in a coating?
o: To act only as evaporating thinner
To provide color, opacity, and selected functional properties
questions.ref: Paint and Coating Testing Manual / architectural coatings terminology; ASTM D16 - Standard Terminology for Paint, Related Coatings, Materials, and Applications
questions.n: Pigments provide color and hiding power and can also contribute corrosion resistance or other performance characteristics.

questions.q: What is embedded in the EIFS base coat to improve impact resistance and crack control?
questions.ref: EIFS Industry Members Association (EIMA), EIFS terminology and system guidance
questions.n: A reinforcing mesh is embedded in the base coat to strengthen the lamina and improve crack/impact resistance.

questions.q: Which standard specifically evaluates perimeter fire barriers between floor assemblies and curtain walls?
questions.ref: ASTM E2307 - Standard Test Method for Determining Fire Resistance of Perimeter Fire Barriers
questions.n: ASTM E2307 evaluates fire resistance of perimeter fire barriers used at exterior curtain wall and floor intersections.

questions.q: A steel roof has been cleaned and primed with a system compatible with galvanized metal. Which finish-coat choice is most appropriate among ordinary building paints?
questions.ref: AMPP/SSPC protective-coatings guidance for metal substrates
questions.n: Exterior metal roofs need coatings designed for weather exposure and compatibility with the prepared metal substrate.
